More full and hopefully even more helpful description of what is going on here.  Sent to clients based on a question about this article 

For anyone who wants to understand the difference between ACM and Kim.  ACM is a PCA model which basically is fully driven by its first two principle components those are level and curve steepness.  I use it but frankly doesn't offer any insight that is useful vs just observing the curve.  Kim adds analyst expectations of rate path.  Because analyst expectations are for a modest or nonexistent and then reversing hiking cycle AND markets are priced for a medium and persistent hiking cycle ACM and curve steepness diverge from Kim. 

OTOH many many factors diverge from Kim including IV and credit spreads and fundamental economic strength and equity prices.  Kim is probably the biggest divergence relative to other indicators of where term premium lies today

Onchain options are the largest remaining whitespace in crypto derivatives.

Most crypto options activity still takes place on centralized venues. Although onchain premium volume recently hit a monthly high, total notional over the past 30 days was still just 4.3% of Deribit’s. Attracting sustained retail flow is the sector’s next hurdle.

Derive currently accounts for roughly 95% of onchain options premium volume. V3 builds on that position by making the same liquidity available across more markets and products.

The existing Derive Chain will be replaced by a zkVM-based system that settles on Ethereum. Its new risk architecture should make it easier to list markets with different risk profiles while portfolio cross-margining improves capital efficiency for traders.

Native vaults could turn those markets into products users access through a single deposit. A covered-call vault could generate income by selling part of a tokenized asset’s upside while creating a more predictable source of flow for market makers.

Consumer apps let users select an asset and express a directional view while Derive handles the options execution underneath. This allows builders to focus on distribution without having to bootstrap a new liquidity venue.

The success of v3 depends on whether these products can attract sustained flow beyond Derive’s existing user base and grow the onchain options market around its infrastructure.

Tokenized equities have historically struggled with liquidity.

Onchain markets often struggle to adjust inventory as demand changes. Backpack lets any user create new token supply from equity positions held in its brokerage and redeem excess tokens back into brokerage positions. This allows liquidity to scale with demand instead of being limited by the tokens already in circulation.

This matters in DeFi because swaps and liquidations depend on liquidity already being available onchain. Backpack’s brokerage gives market makers a way to reliably provide inventory and quote onchain as demand changes. More reliable liquidity can improve execution and make tokenized stocks more practical as collateral.

Across several equities, Backpack delivered the lowest-cost round trip execution compared to other issuer versions.

Backpack’s potential edge lies in the market infrastructure behind its tokens. If execution quality holds as volumes grow, its brokerage could become a durable advantage as onchain equity markets develop.
